data.zone: San Francisco Peaks / Kachina Peaks Wilderness
data.bottom_line: Snowpack Summary: Early Season Update Overall Although winter has started on the San Francisco Peaks, KPAC is not issuing regular avalanche forecasts yet. We will issue snowpack summaries as conditions develop. Snow is currently shallow and spotty. In many places, falling on hidden rocks, stumps and deadfall is a bigger danger right now than an avalanche. That does not mean the snow is stable. Steep, wind-loaded and shaded slopes above treeline can produce small avalanches now, and even a small slide can carry you into rocks and trees or over cliffs. Season so far The Peaks have had several early storms. The first snow came at the end of September and melted within days. A light dusting followed in mid-October. On the night of October 24–25, about 6 inches fell at Snowbowl, and the resort reported about 17 inches of snow before the season started. Another 5 inches fell in mid-November, and Arizona Snowbowl opened a day early, on November 19. After two lean winters, a very strong El Niño is expected to favor the Southwest this season. We hope that’s right, but a promising outlook doesn’t make a good season. What we’re watching Early-season snow thats sitting on shaded, high-elevation slopes through dry, cold spells oftenis turning to weak, sugary facets. If that happens and new snow buries it, it can become a persistent weak layer that lasts deep into the season. We’re watching north- and east-facing terrain near and above treeline closely. Before you go Carry a beacon, shovel and probe and know how to use them. Now is a good time to evaluate your gear with a pre-season checklist . Come to our first Avalanche Awareness this season next Thursday Dec 3rd at the Leaf Auditorium Share what you are seeing even a quick note helps us track conditions. Tag us @kachinapeaksavy , use the AvyApp, or visit our observations page.
